jobs.title: Client Implementation Manager
jobs.description:
Who We Are

KPA helps automotive businesses keep their people safe, protect their operations, and stay ahead of regulatory change with our 3 Pillars for Complete Compliance: Software, Consulting, and Training. Since 1986, KPA has helped automotive businesses navigate the complexities of compliance.

Named as one of Built In Colorado’s Best Places to Work for seven years in a row, KPA is made up of talented individuals working together for the greater good. We’re here to help our clients build safe, thriving organizations, and we’re looking for people with a common goal to help us do it.

About the Role:

A successful customer relationship starts with a strong implementation. At KPA, our Client Implementation Managers play a key role in making that happen, helping new customers get up and running with the tools they need to manage compliance, reduce risk, and operate more effectively.

We're looking for someone who enjoys working directly with customers, solving problems, and bringing structure to complex projects. You'll own the implementation process from initial planning and configuration through training and launch, helping customers navigate challenges and get the most out of KPA's solutions.

This role combines project management, technical problem-solving, and customer relationship management. You'll work closely with customers and internal teams to keep implementations moving forward, resolve roadblocks, and create a positive experience that sets the foundation for long-term success.

What You'll Do:

Own the implementation process. Manage new customer implementations from initial planning and site configuration through training, launch, and transition to ongoing support
Build strong customer relationships. Serve as a trusted point of contact throughout implementation, understanding customer needs, setting expectations, and helping them navigate the process
Keep projects on track. Develop and manage implementation plans, coordinate deliverables, identify potential risks, and proactively address issues that could impact timelines
Configure solutions to meet customer needs. Set up and configure KPA's platforms, providing guidance on product functionality, integrations, and best practices
Solve problems creatively. Work through implementation challenges, identify practical solutions using existing platform capabilities, and help customers overcome obstacles
Help customers become confident users. Train customer administrators and supervisors on how to effectively use KPA's products and manage their environments
Collaborate across teams. Partner with Client Success, Product, and Content teams to troubleshoot issues, share customer feedback, and improve the implementation experience
Set customers up for long-term success. Ensure implementations are completed successfully and customers experience a smooth transition to their ongoing Client Success team

What You'll Bring:

At least 2 years of experience in a customer-facing role, ideally involving customer onboarding, implementation, project coordination, or technical support
Strong organizational and time management skills, with the ability to manage multiple priorities and keep projects moving forward
Confidence communicating with customers, understanding their needs, and guiding conversations toward solutions
A practical, resourceful approach to problem-solving, including the ability to work through unexpected challenges and remove roadblocks
Comfort learning new technology, explaining technical concepts, and helping others become confident using software platforms
The ability to work independently while collaborating effectively with customers and teammates in a remote environment
Experience using Microsoft Office applications and customer relationship management tools
A bachelor's degree or equivalent professional experience

Nice to Have:

Experience working with Salesforce
Previous experience implementing, configuring, or supporting software solutions

What Success Looks Like:

Success in this role goes beyond completing implementations on time. It's about creating an experience where customers feel supported, understand how to use their solutions, and are confident moving forward
You'll be successful when you're able to independently manage implementations, build trust with customers, anticipate challenges before they become larger problems, and work effectively across teams to deliver a smooth onboarding experience
Above all, you'll bring a combination of accountability, curiosity, and a customer-first mindset to your work, helping KPA deliver on its commitment to making compliance simpler and more effective

Compensation:

Base salary of 65-75k commensurate with experience
Annual bonus up to 7.5%

Physical Requirements:

Physical demands described here are representative of those that must be met by an employee to successfully perform the essential functions of this job. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions.

Visual Recognition - Constantly
Stationary sitting or standing position - Constantly
Working at a computer typing and view a screen - Constantly
Speaking, Hearing, and Listening - Often

Studies have shown some people are less likely to apply unless they meet every requirement. If you’re excited about the role but your past experience doesn’t align perfectly with every qualification, we still encourage you to apply! You might just be the right candidate for this or other roles.

As a growing company KPA values its employees by supporting them with a full benefits package including Medical, Dental, Vision, Flexible Spending Accounts, PTO, Paid and Floating Holidays, 401k with Company match and immediate vesting, Company-funded Life Insurance, Employee Assistance Programs, and No-cost Mental Health Benefits.

Promote a strong commitment to safety, quality, teamwork, and continuous improvement.

You'll own a technical workstream, lead working groups that span several organizations, figure out what's really going on, build the plan and drive it to done. Manage risks, issues and decisions.

Help each IC map its existing contracts, end dates and staffing to the consolidation timeline so services transition without gaps.
Deliver in an Agile rhythm.
Plan in sprints, review priorities with stakeholders, and adjust deliverables quickly when client needs change.

:

Bachelor's degree
in IT, engineering, business or a related field, or equivalent experience.
U.S. citizenship
and the ability to obtain and maintain a Public Trust.

NIH, FDA or other federal health agency experience.
If you already know your ICs from your OCIOs and don't need an acronym decoder ring, that's a big plus.
Experience with IT consolidation, shared services or centralization in a large, decentralized organization.
Exposure to federal acquisition: helping an organization think through its contracts, vehicles and transition timing.
Experience as a consultant working alongside government staff and multiple contractors.
PMP or a similar certification. Helpful, but we care more about what you've delivered.

jobs.description:
About Firefly Aerospace

Firefly Aerospace is a space and defense technology company that enables our world to launch, land, and operate in space – anywhere, anytime. As the partner of choice for critical space missions, Firefly is the only commercial company to launch a satellite to orbit with 24-hour notice and the only company to achieve a successful Moon landing. Our launch vehicles, lunar landers, and orbital vehicles provide government and commercial customers with full mission services from low Earth orbit to the Moon and beyond. Headquartered in north Austin, Texas, Firefly is looking for passionate, hardworking innovators to join our team and help fuel our successful trajectory into space.

Summary

Job Description

Eclipse is the medium-lift launch vehicle Firefly is developing with Northrop Grumman. The first flight vehicle is in build today, followed by rate production, and then a path to reusability. Taking a new launch vehicle from first article into rate production is a rare opportunity in this industry, and this role sits at the center of it.

Firefly is seeking a Senior Program Manager to lead execution on Eclipse. This person owns the integrated master schedule, the daily and weekly cadence, and the program's blocker list, serving as the Senior Director's execution partner and the program's most reliable source of ground truth. The work carries real visibility, reaching the CTO and the customer. The role is built to grow, with responsibility expanding as the program does.

Firefly also expects this Program Manager to build the tooling the program runs on: schedule and status dashboards, trackers, and automated reporting, with AI applied to the manual work of status consolidation and schedule analysis so that time goes to clearing blockers rather than producing reports.

The role is based at Firefly's Briggs, TX test and production site, where the hardware is built and tested. Relocation support is available. Candidates who meet most of the qualifications below are encouraged to apply.

Responsibilities

Own the Eclipse integrated master schedule and the critical path to first stage delivery.
Run the execution cadence: daily standups, weekly sprints with must-win deliverables, and task-level tracking down to the manufacturing order.
Clear blockers the day they are raised, and keep the team supplied, informed, and focused.
Set milestone gate criteria and run the gates.
Manage inter-team and customer dependencies so hand-offs do not fail.
Own the tactical risk register and the issues list, and drive both to closure.
Consolidate Engineering, Operations, Supply Chain, Test, and Quality into one program status, including spend and burn tracked with Finance.
Report weekly on progress, velocity, and forecast confidence, and prepare executive and customer status material for the Senior Director.
Give the Senior Director an honest assessment of readiness, progress, and morale.
Build the program's dashboards, trackers, and reporting, applying AI to status consolidation and schedule analysis.
Support planning for the production ramp as the program scales.

Basic Qualifications

Bachelor's degree in engineering or a related technical field, or equivalent experience
8+ years in aerospace program management, technical project leadership, or production program roles
3+ years as a scrum master, agile program manager, or equivalent execution role
Track record of delivering complex technical programs on schedule
Advanced proficiency with MS Project, Smartsheet, Jira, or similar, including critical path method, resource loading, and schedule risk analysis
Command of plan mechanics: how schedule and cost move together, baseline change impacts, where float sits, burn against physical progress
Experience building program tooling, such as dashboards, trackers, or automated reporting
Applied AI in a program execution context, with sound judgment about its limits
Strong facilitation and clear communication with technicians, engineers, and executives
Willingness to provide an honest assessment of program health, including when the news is unwelcome.

DESIRED

Launch vehicle, spacecraft, or comparable complex aerospace development, integration, or test experience
Production ramp or rate scaling experience
Engine or large structures development, qualification, or production
Agile methods applied to hardware development
Scripting, Power BI, or Smartsheet and Jira automation applied to program reporting
Mentoring or developing program management and scheduling talent

Firefly offers outstanding benefits for our employees, including generous health, dental and vision plans with low plan deductibles, parental leave, relocation benefits, educational reimbursement, short term disability, and flexible PTO options.

To conform to U.S. Government space technology export regulations, including the International Traffic in Arms Regulations (ITAR) you must be a U.S. citizen, lawful permanent resident of the U.S., protected individual as defined by 8 U.S.C. 1324b(a)(3), or eligible to obtain the required authorizations from the U.S. Department of State.

Som projektledare ansvarar du för att planera, leda, samordna och följa upp projekt från start till mål. Du säkerställer att projektets mål uppnås inom givna ramar och skapar förutsättningar för att projektteamet ska kunna leverera med hög kvalitet.

Leda projekt genom hela projektets livscykel, från initiering till avslut.
Följa upp projektplan, tidplan, budget och resursplanering.
Säkerställa att projektets mål, leveranser och milstolpar uppnås.

Vi söker dig som har flera års erfarenhet av projektledning i komplexa verksamheter och som är van att ta ansvar för hela projektets genomförande, från planering och uppföljning till leverans och resultat. Du har god kunskap om projektledningsmetodik och förändringsledning samt en förståelse för hur projekt bidrar till verksamhetens övergripande mål. Har du erfarenhet från tekniskt avancerade miljöer eller större organisationer med många beroenden ser vi det som meriterande.

jobs.title: Deployment Strategist
jobs.description:
ReadyOn.AI is an AI-native Labor Operating System that is redefining how the world’s largest enterprises manage frontline labor. Born out of a Stanford AI Lab, the company applies advanced AI and market-design principles to one of the hardest optimization problems on earth: matching the world’s 2.7 billion frontline workers to the right shifts, in real time.

Frontline workers now expect the same flexibility and autonomy that gig platforms provide, while large employers face relentless pressure to meet aggressive labor-cost targets. ReadyOn bridges that divide with a system of action that predicts workforce demand, dynamically matches it to an employer’s supply of employees, and automates the thousands of staffing decisions made daily across complex, multi-site operations.

The platform is already proven at global scale, powering labor operations for several of the world’s largest enterprises. Landmark customers include a F250 food-service enterprise (300K employees across 16 countries; $7B+ annual labor spend, a F500 hotel group (250K+ employees; $5B+ annual labor spend), a F250 entertainment operator (75K employees; $4B+ labor spend). Across these deployments, ReadyOn has proven that scheduling was never the real problem—it was a symptom. The true challenge is how to match people and work dynamically at scale. ReadyOn solves this problem with an AI system of action that transforms labor from a fixed cost into a strategic advantage, reshaping how enterprises think about workforce design altogether.

Headquartered in San Francisco with 80 employees, ReadyOn grew 8x year-over-year revenue growth in 2025, driven by multiple seven-figure Fortune 250 enterprise deployments and a rapidly expanding pipeline.

Transform How Frontline Work Runs

Enterprises struggle to manage hundreds of millions of dollars in frontline labor spend due to decades-old software and manual processes, creating massive, avoidable costs. Frontline labor often represents 40% of the P&L, yet the systems managing this $3 trillion market were built for static schedules and limited flexibility.

ReadyOn was founded to reject that paradigm. Staffing is not a scheduling problem; it is a real-time supply–demand orchestration problem. ReadyOn is an AI-native labor operating system, built from the ground up for AI agents to perform real-time labor optimization - much like ridesharing platforms that match drivers and riders in real time, but applied to frontline labor instead of fixed, one-size-fits-all schedules.

Who’s Building It

AI is not a bolt-on feature in our platform. Every decision, from demand forecasting to shift assignment, flows through an adaptive, autonomous decision layer that learns from operational data and continuously optimizes for cost, compliance, and worker satisfaction. Behind that system is a founding team of experts in labor markets, enterprise software, and AI-enabled platforms:

Reza – Engineering leader who scaled enterprise systems at Google, Yahoo, and AT&T
Dominic – Operator who optimized labor-intensive operations in 21 countries
Mohammad – Stanford professor and leading expert in algorithmic market design

ReadyOn has already proven product–market fit with multiple multi-million-dollar customers, consistent expansion within existing accounts, and measurable ROI that moves stock prices.

Deployment Strategist Role

Joining the Enterprise Partnerships team, the Deployment Strategist works across multiple customer deployments and alongside our Engagement Managers to turn complex labor environments into working ReadyOn deployments. You will contribute directly to live Fortune 500 implementations: building configurations, running data analyses, supporting training delivery, and joining customer engagements.

You will also build the structured product intelligence that helps Engineering and Product understand what is happening in the field. The best people in this role become the team’s institutional memory, and the role grows from deployment execution into product synthesis, analytical infrastructure, and solutions work. Strong performers move into Engagement Management, Solutions Engineering, or Product roles.

Ideal Candidates:

Learn by Doing: You get up to speed quickly in unfamiliar tools, data, and operating environments, and you are comfortable contributing to live Fortune 500 deployments from day one.
Turn Data into Decisions: You break down ambiguous operational questions, work directly with messy data, and move quickly from analysis to a clear recommendation.
Own Your Workstreams: You take ownership of multiple workstreams at once, work out what needs to happen next, and follow through without close supervision.
Build for Reuse: You look for the template, script, or playbook that makes the next deployment faster than the last, and you build it.
Be the Bridge: You explain technical and analytical findings clearly to engineers, product managers, and non-technical operators, and you turn what you see in the field into structured product feedback.

Responsibilities & Impact

Execute Client Deployments: Own defined deployment workstreams, including go-live preparation, configuration troubleshooting, and manager training. Lead relevant client calls and bring technical and analytical depth to customer conversations.
Design Configurations and Solutions: Translate employer data and rules into system-ready configurations. Own solution design details in pilots and early-stage deployments, and contribute to validation and UAT testing.
Turn Field Insight into Product Direction: Surface field-level product gaps to Product and Engineering, grounded in deployment data. Write feature requests informed by cross-customer pattern analysis.
Deliver Data Analysis and Reporting: Build deployment health dashboards, cross-customer operational analyses, and adoption and usage metrics. Run ad hoc data pulls for customer-facing deliverables such as board decks and QBR materials.
Automate and Reuse: Build reusable templates, scripts, playbooks, and analytical frameworks that make each subsequent deployment faster, and support the data warehouse and internal analytics infrastructure as it develops.

Your Background

0-3 years of professional experience, with a degree in Computer Science, Economics, Business, Data Analytics, Mathematics, Engineering, or a similar analytical field.
Analytical Problem-Solving and Data Fluency: You structure ambiguous operational questions into analyses, work comfortably with raw data (exports, API responses, unfamiliar schemas), and spot patterns across data sets and engagements.
Technical Orientation: You pick up new tools and schemas quickly, think in systems, and have basic comfort with code: you can read scripts, automate repetitive tasks, and debug configurations. You know enough about APIs, data sync, and webhooks to diagnose problems and talk with engineers.
Execution and Operational Rigor: You manage several concurrent workstreams, follow through without close supervision, and build repeatable processes that make the team more consistent.

jobs.title: 35F Intelligence Analyst
jobs.description:
Job Description

On the battlefield, success depends on accurate and timely intel. As an Army National Guard Intelligence Analyst, you will play a key role in the interpretation and exploitation of information gathered from or about the threat. Intelligence Analysts provide Guard personnel with information about enemy forces and potential battle areas, and use information derived from all intelligence disciplines to determine changes in enemy capabilities, vulnerabilities, and probable courses of action. You’ll gain Military Intelligence training, education, and a security clearance that could open doors to rewarding career opportunities with other intelligence agencies.

Specific duties of the Intelligence Analyst may include: preparing all-source intelligence products; providing Intelligence, Surveillance, and Reconnaissance (ISR) Synchronization support; processing incoming reports and messages; determining the significance and reliability of incoming information; establishing and maintaining systematic, cross-referencing intelligence records and files; integrating incoming information with current intelligence holdings; and preparing and maintaining enemy situational graphics.

Job Duties

Preparing all-source intelligence products to support the combat commander
Assessing the significance and reliability of incoming intelligence collection
Establishing and maintaining systematic, cross-reference intelligence records and files

Some Of The Skills You’ll Learn

Critical thinking
The ability to use sophisticated mapping tools, intelligence networks, and systems to identify the evolving threat on the battlefield
Gather information utilizing premier digital and analytical tools to create products for the Commander

Helpful Skills

Analytical thinking; gathering information, and understanding of relevancy
Interest in reading maps and charts

More than any other branch of service, the Army National Guard offers a wide range of intelligence-related positions. Through your training, you will develop skills and experience to create opportunities for a civilian career with federal agencies like the National Security Agency.

Earn While You Learn

Instead of paying to learn these skills, get paid to learn. In the Army National Guard, you will learn these valuable job skills while earning a regular paycheck and qualifying for tuition assistance and certifications. Job training for an Intelligence Analyst consists of 10 weeks of Basic Training, where you'll learn basic Soldiering skills, and 13 weeks of Advanced Individual Training (AIT) and on-the-job instruction, including practice in intelligence gathering. You’ll learn in the classroom and gain experience in the field. Completion of your initial entry training in the Army National Guard could also lead to additional college credit.

Benefits/Requirements

Benefits

Paid training
Earn a security clearance
A monthly paycheck
Montgomery GI Bill
Federal and State tuition assistance
Retirement benefits for part-time service
Low-cost life insurance (up to $400,000 in coverage)
401(k)-type savings plan
Student Loan Repayment Program (up to $50,000, for existing loans)
Health care benefits available
VA home loans
Bonuses, if applicable

Most non-prior service candidates will initially earn between $200 and $250 per drill weekend, subject to change.

Requirements

Military enlistment in the Army National Guard
Must be at least a junior in high school, or have a high school diploma or GED certificate
Must be between the ages of 17 and 35
Must be able to pass a physical exam and meet legal and moral standards
Must meet citizenship requirements (see NATIONALGUARD.com for details)

Requires military enlistment. Programs and benefits are subject to change. Ask your Army National Guard recruiter for the most up-to-date information. Actual MOS assignment may depend on MOS availability.

jobs.title: Data Analyst, Client Insights
jobs.description:
About RK Media

RK Media is a dynamic organization representing Christian non-profit ministries who use radio, television, podcasts and digital media to reach their audience. As a full-service agency, we serve our ministry partners through the production of top-quality Bible teaching, talk and inspirational broadcasts and podcasts that include strategic fundraising campaigns and promotions. We also serve as the direct liaison between non-profit ministries, the radio stations and other outlets that carry their programs.
RK Media offers a fast-paced, collaborative work environment with potential for both personal and professional growth. We value individuals who wish to make a direct impact in the mission of Christian non-profit ministries through the media industry. We believe that when team members find value and meaning in their work, they experience success and significance. Learn more at rkmedia.co.

The role

We're hiring a data analyst who loves digging into numbers, telling the story behind the numbers, and wants to help ministries understand what's working.

Most of your time (~ 70%) goes to analysis: building and owning reporting for our ministry partners, managing our internal data, and creating cross-ministry benchmarks. Approximately 20% is working with the people behind the requests. That means joining ministry partner calls when needed, finding out why someone is asking for a report, and coming back with more than they asked for.
This is a role for a self-starter. We're looking for someone who takes initiative, solves problems without waiting to be told exactly what to do, brings a "yes, and" attitude, and keeps everyone clear on expectations.

What you'll do

Reporting and analysis (about 70%)

Take over and improve RK's current reporting for ministry partners, including monthly financial reports, station data requests, and social media analytics reports.
Turn one-off client reports into a consistent RK reporting service that partners can rely on.
Fully own RK's cross-ministry benchmarks, with feedback from senior leadership: what "good" looks like by channel, and how each ministry compares.
Build those benchmarks into partner reports, so every ministry understands their experience in a broader context.
Manage and organize RK's internal data: understand what data we have, where it lives, and how to keep it clean and usable.
Present data-backed recommendations across various channels.
As recurring reporting is automated, expect more of your time to shift toward analysis and projects across RK

Client insight (about 20%)

Join client calls as needed alongside the Media Services team.
Dig past the direct request: understand what led to it and where the ministry is headed.
Support the account lead in assessing how a report furthers a ministry’s impact.

Other (about 10%)

Take part in internal team meetings, planning sessions, and company-wide meetings.
Keep building your skills through training, new tools, and learning the ministry media landscape, with RK’s support.
As reporting becomes more automated, take on data projects for other RK teams, such as campaign performance analysis for Digital Marketing, station and affiliate data for Station Relations, or operational and financial analysis for leadership.
Help find other manual processes across RK that could be simplified or automated.
Other duties as assigned.

Who you'll work with

You'll work mainly with the Media Services team, which includes Station Relations and Digital Marketing. Over time there's room to grow into work with all of our teams.

What success looks like

In your first 90 days

You know our ministry partners, their goals, and the reports we provide each of them.
You've taken over the current reporting process, including the quarterly social media reports.
You've mapped what data RK has, where it lives, who owns it, and how it's collected.
You've joined client calls with the Media Services team and built working relationships with the account leads.

By 6 months

You've recommended how to elevate RK's reporting, and we've agreed on a plan.
You've proposed a standard set of metrics and a consistent report format across ministries.
You've set up how client data is organized and protected, so cross-ministry benchmarking can be done responsibly.
Account leads bring you into client conversations because your recommendations go beyond the original request.

By 1 year

Standardized reporting with benchmarks is running as a new service for our ministry partners, allowing them to see how their experience fits within a larger ministry context. 
RK's data and reporting processes are documented and repeatable.
You’ve elevated reporting both internally and for our clients.

What you bring

Required

3–5 years of experience in data analysis, marketing analytics, reporting, or a similar role.
Well versed in using AI tools, such as Claude, in your daily work. 
Comfortable in Excel: pivot tables, lookups, and cleaning and combining messy data. You genuinely enjoy working in spreadsheets.
A track record of presenting findings and recommendations to non-technical audiences.
Clear, concise writing — you can explain what the data means and what to do about it.
Initiative: you find answers and solve problems without needing step-by-step direction.
Strong communication and people skills, including asking good questions and setting clear expectations.
Sound judgment with confidential information.
A general understanding of Christian denominational and theological differences, and empathy for the mission of non-profit ministries.

Preferred

Bachelor's degree, or trade school or certificate training, in a related field.
Experience with nonprofit fundraising, direct response, media buying, or donor data.
Familiarity with radio, podcast, or social media metrics.
Experience with SQL, or with a BI tool such as Power BI or Tableau. Experience setting up or managing a database.
Experience working with multiple clients/accounts at once.

Work environment and pay

Schedule:
In our Westlake Village office Tuesday through Thursday. Monday and Friday you can work from home or come into the office. Hours are 8:00 a.m.–5:00 p.m. Pacific.
Travel:
Occasional partner visits and an industry conference, up to about 5%.
Pay:
$80-$95K BOE
Benefits:
Health, dental and vision insurance; FSA; life insurance; 401(k) Safe Harbor plan during open enrollment after one year; 15 days of paid time off; 5 sick days; and paid holidays.
Equipment:
Laptop and monitor provided in the office.

How to apply

Submit your resume, a cover letter (required; one page maximum)
, and answers to the application questions. Applications without a cover letter won't be considered.

We are Toshiba. We have an unwavering drive to make and do things that lead to a better world.

Founded in 1965, Toshiba America, Inc. (TAI) is a subsidiary of the globally renowned Toshiba Corporation based in Tokyo. As the holding company for three Toshiba operating companies, TAI offers a wide array of products and solutions across the commercial, energy, and industrial sectors. Together with our subsidiaries, we form the Toshiba Americas Group, which is committed to technological innovation and excellence.

Our Commitment to the Future

At Toshiba America, we are guided by the principle “Committed to People, Committed to the Future.” This core philosophy shapes our strategies and actions as we strive to build a better, more sustainable world. In an era of climate change, resource depletion, and social inequality, we aim to ensure safety, security, and environmental stability for all.

Job Summary

We are seeking a skilled and motivated mid-level Cybersecurity Analyst to help strengthen our defenses against evolving cyber threats. In this role, you will monitor, investigate, and respond to security events while also contributing to long-term security improvements. The ideal candidate has proven experience, takes ownership of incident response, and can work across teams to drive results.

Key Responsibilities

Monitor, analyze, and investigate security events, alerts, and incidents to identify threats and anomalies
Act as a primary responder during security incidents, handling detection, analysis, triage, containment, eradication, and recovery
Conduct root cause analysis and document findings for leadership review
Perform vulnerability assessments, coordinate with teams, and drive remediation efforts
Support proactive threat hunting and detection of suspicious activities
Assist in configuring, maintaining, and tuning security tools, including firewalls, IDS/IPS, EDR, and email security platforms
Contribute to security and compliance initiatives (ISO 27001, NIST CSF, Zero Trust) and internal audits
Support security awareness campaigns and phishing defense programs
Recommend improvements to tools, processes, and playbooks
Develop and refine runbooks, procedures, and standards to improve SOC efficiency
Research emerging threats, attack vectors, AI related risks and industry standards to keep defenses current
Develop, implement, and enforce security policies, procedures, and best practices
Apply strong problem-solving skills to handle moderately complex incidents

Qualifications

4–6 years of hands-on experience in cybersecurity, SOC, or information security roles
Strong knowledge of network protocols (TCP/IP), operating systems (Windows, Linux), and core security concepts
Familiarity with attack techniques, endpoint protection, malware behavior, and cloud defense strategies
Proven experience using SIEM platforms, writing queries, and analyzing alerts
Awareness of AI security risks (e.g., model manipulation, data poisoning, prompt injection) and willingness to learn and apply best practices in securing AI-driven systems
Demonstrated ability to perform root cause analysis and explain findings to both technical and non-technical audiences
Experience automating repetitive tasks and scripting for analysis or reporting
Familiarity with log analysis and query languages
Hands-on experience with threat hunting methodologies
Excellent communication skills

The Analyst, Research & Quality contributes to a broad portfolio spanning clinical practice guidelines (CPGs), expert consensus statements (ECSs), clinical research, registry analytics, and quality improvement. Working with physician experts, Academy staff, and technical partners, the Analyst helps move evidence into practice through guideline development, digitization of recommendations, and data-informed tools. This role offers opportunities to develop skills across evidence synthesis, health informatics, and applied analytics. Success requires curiosity, sound judgment, initiative, adaptability, and the aptitude to learn unfamiliar methods and technology.

The Analyst, Research & Quality reports to the VP, Research & Quality and works closely with the Senior Data Scientist and Senior Program Manager.

Key Responsibilities

Clinical Practice Guidelines & Expert Consensus Statements

Support physician panels, Academy staff, and methodology partners across CPG and ECS development, learning established evidence-based processes.
Assist with literature searches, screening, evidence tables, reference management, and concise summaries of clinical research.
Help coordinate evidence review, panel feedback, consensus activities (including Delphi surveys), drafting, and revisions.
Track milestones and documentation; support manuscripts, publication submissions, and dissemination materials.

Research Data Analysis & Registry Support

Work with the Senior Data Scientist to turn clinical and operational questions into feasible data requests and analytic deliverables.
Develop and refine SQL queries, with guidance as needed, to identify cohorts, connect records, and calculate measures.
Use or develop skills in Python or R to clean, validate, summarize, and analyze data using reproducible approaches.
Check data completeness and consistency, investigate unexpected findings, and document limitations and questions for review.
Prepare clear tables, figures, dashboards, and summaries for technical and nontechnical audiences.
Explore practical improvements in data quality checks, workflow efficiency, automation, and registry-based research.

Reg-ENT Research, Innovation & Collaboration

Assist with feasibility assessments for research proposals, including cohort definitions, available data, and analytic needs; support RAPID review and tracking.
Contribute to registry research, grants, industry collaborations, and quality initiatives through analyses and concise presentations.
Help translate CPG key action statements into structured concepts, clinical terminology, coding logic, and measurable data elements for digital implementation.
Assist participating Reg-ent practices with interpreting registry measures, trends, dashboards, and data-quality questions.

Communications & Project Support

Draft accessible research summaries, presentation materials, manuscript content, and project updates.
Maintain clear documentation of methods, data definitions, code, decisions, and project versions.
Coordinate assigned meetings and deliverables, proactively flagging questions, dependencies, and risks.
May participate in evening calls or weekend meetings supporting committees and guideline/consensus development groups.
Contribute to cross-functional initiatives and support AAO-HNS/F committees as assigned.
Build effective relationships with clinicians, members, industry collaborators, and colleagues; suggest improvements and learn from feedback.
Other duties as assigned.

Qualifications

Bachelor’s degree in public health, epidemiology, health informatics, computer science, data science, statistics, or a related field required. Relevant coursework, projects, internships, or professional experience may demonstrate preparation for this early-career role; graduate education is welcome but not required.
Foundational qualifications: Strong analytical reasoning, research and information-literacy skills, attention to detail, and clear written and verbal communication. Ability to organize complex work, investigate discrepancies, manage competing priorities, ask thoughtful questions, and learn new tools quickly. Comfort working with data and spreadsheets (including Excel) and an interest in developing technical and methodological expertise.
Desired experience or exposure (not all required): Clinical practice guidelines, evidence reviews, literature searching, or consensus methods; SQL and/or Python or R; data visualization and descriptive statistics; electronic health records, clinical registries, and healthcare terminology or coding systems (such as ICD-10, CPT, or SNOMED CT); digital health, structured clinical content, automation, or AI-assisted workflows. Demonstrated aptitude and willingness to learn are valued alongside direct experience. Ability to work independently and collaboratively. Some evening meetings, weekend work, and travel may be required.

iVision Consulting is looking for a hands-on Technical Project Manager to help grow our Federal IT Transformation work. You'll team up with our senior advisors and NIH's executive leadership on one of the bigger IT efforts in federal health: centralizing foundational IT services across the National Institutes of Health (NIH) and its Institutes and Centers. This is not a take-notes-and-update-the-tracker job. You'll own a technical workstream, lead working groups that span several organizations, figure out what's really going on, build the plan and drive it to done. Your work will get a lot of eyes from IT, governance, acquisition and workforce leaders, so it needs to be clear and solid. If you like untangling dependencies and getting people to the finish line together, keep reading.

Candidate must be a U.S. Citizen and be able to obtain a Public Trust. This is a hybrid position and is required to be onsite 2-3 days per week in Bethesda, Maryland.

Must have PMP certification.

What You Will Do:

In this role, you take charge of your workstream and keep the organization moving with it. You’ll set direction, bring the right people to the table, and turn complex technical work into steady, visible progress. Here’s what that looks like day to day.

Own a consolidation workstream end to end.
Take full responsibility for a workstream such as network, data center and hosting, or help desk, from discovery through cutover and handoff to the receiving organization.
Run discovery with the Institutes and Centers.
Plan and facilitate working sessions to inventory each IC's infrastructure, applications, networks, support staff and contracts. Turn what you learn into current-state documentation and a clear list of decisions needed.
Build and own the integrated schedule.
Develop detailed schedules that cover migration waves, test cycles, cutover windows, readiness gates and handoffs. Keep the baseline current and the critical path visible.
Surface and manage technical dependencies.
Identify where systems, teams and contracts depend on each other, sequence the work to match, and resolve conflicts before they put a cutover at risk.
Review technical artifacts.
Evaluate network diagrams, architecture documents, application inventories, migration plans and vendor deliverables. Flag gaps, risks and unrealistic assumptions, and push for fixes.
Lead multi-organization working groups.
Run recurring sessions with engineers, IC IT staff, and governance, acquisition and workforce stakeholders. Drive decisions, assign owners and follow up until every action closes.
Manage risks, issues and decisions.
Keep risk and issue registers and decision logs current. Escalate early, with options and a recommendation.
Connect acquisition and workforce planning to the schedule.
Help each IC map its existing contracts, end dates and staffing to the consolidation timeline so services transition without gaps.
Deliver in an Agile rhythm.

24/7 Security Operations Center; immutable backups; isolated recovery environments; practiced, repeatable recoveries

new_jobs.description:
About Firefly Aerospace

Firefly Aerospace is a space and defense technology company that enables our world to launch, land, and operate in space – anywhere, anytime. As the partner of choice for critical space missions, Firefly is the only commercial company to launch a satellite to orbit with 24-hour notice and the only company to achieve a successful Moon landing. Our launch vehicles, lunar landers, and orbital vehicles provide government and commercial customers with full mission services from low Earth orbit to the Moon and beyond. Headquartered in north Austin, Texas, Firefly is looking for passionate, hardworking innovators to join our team and help fuel our successful trajectory into space.

Summary

Job Description

Eclipse is the medium-lift launch vehicle Firefly is developing with Northrop Grumman. The first flight vehicle is in build today, followed by rate production, and then a path to reusability. Taking a new launch vehicle from first article into rate production is a rare opportunity in this industry, and this role sits at the center of it.

Firefly is seeking a Senior Program Manager to lead execution on Eclipse. This person owns the integrated master schedule, the daily and weekly cadence, and the program's blocker list, serving as the Senior Director's execution partner and the program's most reliable source of ground truth. The work carries real visibility, reaching the CTO and the customer. The role is built to grow, with responsibility expanding as the program does.

Firefly also expects this Program Manager to build the tooling the program runs on: schedule and status dashboards, trackers, and automated reporting, with AI applied to the manual work of status consolidation and schedule analysis so that time goes to clearing blockers rather than producing reports.

The role is based at Firefly's Briggs, TX test and production site, where the hardware is built and tested. Relocation support is available. Candidates who meet most of the qualifications below are encouraged to apply.

Responsibilities

Own the Eclipse integrated master schedule and the critical path to first stage delivery.
Run the execution cadence: daily standups, weekly sprints with must-win deliverables, and task-level tracking down to the manufacturing order.
Clear blockers the day they are raised, and keep the team supplied, informed, and focused.
Set milestone gate criteria and run the gates.
Manage inter-team and customer dependencies so hand-offs do not fail.
Own the tactical risk register and the issues list, and drive both to closure.
Consolidate Engineering, Operations, Supply Chain, Test, and Quality into one program status, including spend and burn tracked with Finance.
Report weekly on progress, velocity, and forecast confidence, and prepare executive and customer status material for the Senior Director.
Give the Senior Director an honest assessment of readiness, progress, and morale.
Build the program's dashboards, trackers, and reporting, applying AI to status consolidation and schedule analysis.
Support planning for the production ramp as the program scales.

Basic Qualifications

Bachelor's degree in engineering or a related technical field, or equivalent experience
8+ years in aerospace program management, technical project leadership, or production program roles
3+ years as a scrum master, agile program manager, or equivalent execution role
Track record of delivering complex technical programs on schedule
Advanced proficiency with MS Project, Smartsheet, Jira, or similar, including critical path method, resource loading, and schedule risk analysis
Command of plan mechanics: how schedule and cost move together, baseline change impacts, where float sits, burn against physical progress
Experience building program tooling, such as dashboards, trackers, or automated reporting
Applied AI in a program execution context, with sound judgment about its limits
Strong facilitation and clear communication with technicians, engineers, and executives
Willingness to provide an honest assessment of program health, including when the news is unwelcome.

DESIRED

Launch vehicle, spacecraft, or comparable complex aerospace development, integration, or test experience
Production ramp or rate scaling experience
Engine or large structures development, qualification, or production
Agile methods applied to hardware development
Scripting, Power BI, or Smartsheet and Jira automation applied to program reporting
Mentoring or developing program management and scheduling talent

Firefly offers outstanding benefits for our employees, including generous health, dental and vision plans with low plan deductibles, parental leave, relocation benefits, educational reimbursement, short term disability, and flexible PTO options.

To conform to U.S. Government space technology export regulations, including the International Traffic in Arms Regulations (ITAR) you must be a U.S. citizen, lawful permanent resident of the U.S., protected individual as defined by 8 U.S.C. 1324b(a)(3), or eligible to obtain the required authorizations from the U.S. Department of State.

new_jobs.title: Deployment Strategist
new_jobs.description:
ReadyOn.AI is an AI-native Labor Operating System that is redefining how the world’s largest enterprises manage frontline labor. Born out of a Stanford AI Lab, the company applies advanced AI and market-design principles to one of the hardest optimization problems on earth: matching the world’s 2.7 billion frontline workers to the right shifts, in real time.

Frontline workers now expect the same flexibility and autonomy that gig platforms provide, while large employers face relentless pressure to meet aggressive labor-cost targets. ReadyOn bridges that divide with a system of action that predicts workforce demand, dynamically matches it to an employer’s supply of employees, and automates the thousands of staffing decisions made daily across complex, multi-site operations.

The platform is already proven at global scale, powering labor operations for several of the world’s largest enterprises. Landmark customers include a F250 food-service enterprise (300K employees across 16 countries; $7B+ annual labor spend, a F500 hotel group (250K+ employees; $5B+ annual labor spend), a F250 entertainment operator (75K employees; $4B+ labor spend). Across these deployments, ReadyOn has proven that scheduling was never the real problem—it was a symptom. The true challenge is how to match people and work dynamically at scale. ReadyOn solves this problem with an AI system of action that transforms labor from a fixed cost into a strategic advantage, reshaping how enterprises think about workforce design altogether.

Headquartered in San Francisco with 80 employees, ReadyOn grew 8x year-over-year revenue growth in 2025, driven by multiple seven-figure Fortune 250 enterprise deployments and a rapidly expanding pipeline.

Transform How Frontline Work Runs

Enterprises struggle to manage hundreds of millions of dollars in frontline labor spend due to decades-old software and manual processes, creating massive, avoidable costs. Frontline labor often represents 40% of the P&L, yet the systems managing this $3 trillion market were built for static schedules and limited flexibility.

ReadyOn was founded to reject that paradigm. Staffing is not a scheduling problem; it is a real-time supply–demand orchestration problem. ReadyOn is an AI-native labor operating system, built from the ground up for AI agents to perform real-time labor optimization - much like ridesharing platforms that match drivers and riders in real time, but applied to frontline labor instead of fixed, one-size-fits-all schedules.

Who’s Building It

AI is not a bolt-on feature in our platform. Every decision, from demand forecasting to shift assignment, flows through an adaptive, autonomous decision layer that learns from operational data and continuously optimizes for cost, compliance, and worker satisfaction. Behind that system is a founding team of experts in labor markets, enterprise software, and AI-enabled platforms:

Reza – Engineering leader who scaled enterprise systems at Google, Yahoo, and AT&T
Dominic – Operator who optimized labor-intensive operations in 21 countries
Mohammad – Stanford professor and leading expert in algorithmic market design

ReadyOn has already proven product–market fit with multiple multi-million-dollar customers, consistent expansion within existing accounts, and measurable ROI that moves stock prices.

Deployment Strategist Role

Joining the Enterprise Partnerships team, the Deployment Strategist works across multiple customer deployments and alongside our Engagement Managers to turn complex labor environments into working ReadyOn deployments. You will contribute directly to live Fortune 500 implementations: building configurations, running data analyses, supporting training delivery, and joining customer engagements.

You will also build the structured product intelligence that helps Engineering and Product understand what is happening in the field. The best people in this role become the team’s institutional memory, and the role grows from deployment execution into product synthesis, analytical infrastructure, and solutions work. Strong performers move into Engagement Management, Solutions Engineering, or Product roles.

Ideal Candidates:

Learn by Doing: You get up to speed quickly in unfamiliar tools, data, and operating environments, and you are comfortable contributing to live Fortune 500 deployments from day one.
Turn Data into Decisions: You break down ambiguous operational questions, work directly with messy data, and move quickly from analysis to a clear recommendation.
Own Your Workstreams: You take ownership of multiple workstreams at once, work out what needs to happen next, and follow through without close supervision.
Build for Reuse: You look for the template, script, or playbook that makes the next deployment faster than the last, and you build it.
Be the Bridge: You explain technical and analytical findings clearly to engineers, product managers, and non-technical operators, and you turn what you see in the field into structured product feedback.

Responsibilities & Impact

Execute Client Deployments: Own defined deployment workstreams, including go-live preparation, configuration troubleshooting, and manager training. Lead relevant client calls and bring technical and analytical depth to customer conversations.
Design Configurations and Solutions: Translate employer data and rules into system-ready configurations. Own solution design details in pilots and early-stage deployments, and contribute to validation and UAT testing.
Turn Field Insight into Product Direction: Surface field-level product gaps to Product and Engineering, grounded in deployment data. Write feature requests informed by cross-customer pattern analysis.
Deliver Data Analysis and Reporting: Build deployment health dashboards, cross-customer operational analyses, and adoption and usage metrics. Run ad hoc data pulls for customer-facing deliverables such as board decks and QBR materials.
Automate and Reuse: Build reusable templates, scripts, playbooks, and analytical frameworks that make each subsequent deployment faster, and support the data warehouse and internal analytics infrastructure as it develops.

Your Background

0-3 years of professional experience, with a degree in Computer Science, Economics, Business, Data Analytics, Mathematics, Engineering, or a similar analytical field.
Analytical Problem-Solving and Data Fluency: You structure ambiguous operational questions into analyses, work comfortably with raw data (exports, API responses, unfamiliar schemas), and spot patterns across data sets and engagements.
Technical Orientation: You pick up new tools and schemas quickly, think in systems, and have basic comfort with code: you can read scripts, automate repetitive tasks, and debug configurations. You know enough about APIs, data sync, and webhooks to diagnose problems and talk with engineers.
Execution and Operational Rigor: You manage several concurrent workstreams, follow through without close supervision, and build repeatable processes that make the team more consistent.
Internal and External Communication: You distill complex information clearly on client calls and write summaries, feature requests, and status updates that stand on their own. You work well across engineering, product, and customer teams.
AI-assisted development tools: Claude Code, Cursor, nice to have: Python or BI tool experience
Nice to Have: Exposure to enterprise SaaS, workforce management, or labor operations.

new_jobs.title: 35F Intelligence Analyst
new_jobs.description:
Job Description

On the battlefield, success depends on accurate and timely intel. As an Army National Guard Intelligence Analyst, you will play a key role in the interpretation and exploitation of information gathered from or about the threat. Intelligence Analysts provide Guard personnel with information about enemy forces and potential battle areas, and use information derived from all intelligence disciplines to determine changes in enemy capabilities, vulnerabilities, and probable courses of action. You’ll gain Military Intelligence training, education, and a security clearance that could open doors to rewarding career opportunities with other intelligence agencies.

Specific duties of the Intelligence Analyst may include: preparing all-source intelligence products; providing Intelligence, Surveillance, and Reconnaissance (ISR) Synchronization support; processing incoming reports and messages; determining the significance and reliability of incoming information; establishing and maintaining systematic, cross-referencing intelligence records and files; integrating incoming information with current intelligence holdings; and preparing and maintaining enemy situational graphics.

Job Duties

Preparing all-source intelligence products to support the combat commander
Assessing the significance and reliability of incoming intelligence collection
Establishing and maintaining systematic, cross-reference intelligence records and files

Some Of The Skills You’ll Learn

Critical thinking
The ability to use sophisticated mapping tools, intelligence networks, and systems to identify the evolving threat on the battlefield
Gather information utilizing premier digital and analytical tools to create products for the Commander

Helpful Skills

Analytical thinking; gathering information, and understanding of relevancy
Interest in reading maps and charts

More than any other branch of service, the Army National Guard offers a wide range of intelligence-related positions. Through your training, you will develop skills and experience to create opportunities for a civilian career with federal agencies like the National Security Agency.

Earn While You Learn

Instead of paying to learn these skills, get paid to learn. In the Army National Guard, you will learn these valuable job skills while earning a regular paycheck and qualifying for tuition assistance and certifications. Job training for an Intelligence Analyst consists of 10 weeks of Basic Training, where you'll learn basic Soldiering skills, and 13 weeks of Advanced Individual Training (AIT) and on-the-job instruction, including practice in intelligence gathering. You’ll learn in the classroom and gain experience in the field. Completion of your initial entry training in the Army National Guard could also lead to additional college credit.

Benefits/Requirements

Benefits

Paid training
Earn a security clearance
A monthly paycheck
Montgomery GI Bill
Federal and State tuition assistance
Retirement benefits for part-time service
Low-cost life insurance (up to $400,000 in coverage)
401(k)-type savings plan
Student Loan Repayment Program (up to $50,000, for existing loans)
Health care benefits available
VA home loans
Bonuses, if applicable

Most non-prior service candidates will initially earn between $200 and $250 per drill weekend, subject to change.

Requirements

Military enlistment in the Army National Guard
Must be at least a junior in high school, or have a high school diploma or GED certificate
Must be between the ages of 17 and 35
Must be able to pass a physical exam and meet legal and moral standards
Must meet citizenship requirements (see NATIONALGUARD.com for details)

Requires military enlistment. Programs and benefits are subject to change. Ask your Army National Guard recruiter for the most up-to-date information. Actual MOS assignment may depend on MOS availability.

new_jobs.title: Data Analyst, Client Insights
new_jobs.description:
About RK Media

RK Media is a dynamic organization representing Christian non-profit ministries who use radio, television, podcasts and digital media to reach their audience. As a full-service agency, we serve our ministry partners through the production of top-quality Bible teaching, talk and inspirational broadcasts and podcasts that include strategic fundraising campaigns and promotions. We also serve as the direct liaison between non-profit ministries, the radio stations and other outlets that carry their programs.
RK Media offers a fast-paced, collaborative work environment with potential for both personal and professional growth. We value individuals who wish to make a direct impact in the mission of Christian non-profit ministries through the media industry. We believe that when team members find value and meaning in their work, they experience success and significance. Learn more at rkmedia.co.

The role

We're hiring a data analyst who loves digging into numbers, telling the story behind the numbers, and wants to help ministries understand what's working.

Most of your time (~ 70%) goes to analysis: building and owning reporting for our ministry partners, managing our internal data, and creating cross-ministry benchmarks. Approximately 20% is working with the people behind the requests. That means joining ministry partner calls when needed, finding out why someone is asking for a report, and coming back with more than they asked for.
This is a role for a self-starter. We're looking for someone who takes initiative, solves problems without waiting to be told exactly what to do, brings a "yes, and" attitude, and keeps everyone clear on expectations.

What you'll do

Reporting and analysis (about 70%)

Take over and improve RK's current reporting for ministry partners, including monthly financial reports, station data requests, and social media analytics reports.
Turn one-off client reports into a consistent RK reporting service that partners can rely on.
Fully own RK's cross-ministry benchmarks, with feedback from senior leadership: what "good" looks like by channel, and how each ministry compares.
Build those benchmarks into partner reports, so every ministry understands their experience in a broader context.
Manage and organize RK's internal data: understand what data we have, where it lives, and how to keep it clean and usable.
Present data-backed recommendations across various channels.
As recurring reporting is automated, expect more of your time to shift toward analysis and projects across RK

Client insight (about 20%)

Join client calls as needed alongside the Media Services team.
Dig past the direct request: understand what led to it and where the ministry is headed.
Support the account lead in assessing how a report furthers a ministry’s impact.

Other (about 10%)

Take part in internal team meetings, planning sessions, and company-wide meetings.
Keep building your skills through training, new tools, and learning the ministry media landscape, with RK’s support.
As reporting becomes more automated, take on data projects for other RK teams, such as campaign performance analysis for Digital Marketing, station and affiliate data for Station Relations, or operational and financial analysis for leadership.
Help find other manual processes across RK that could be simplified or automated.
Other duties as assigned.

Who you'll work with

You'll work mainly with the Media Services team, which includes Station Relations and Digital Marketing. Over time there's room to grow into work with all of our teams.

What success looks like

In your first 90 days

You know our ministry partners, their goals, and the reports we provide each of them.
You've taken over the current reporting process, including the quarterly social media reports.
You've mapped what data RK has, where it lives, who owns it, and how it's collected.
You've joined client calls with the Media Services team and built working relationships with the account leads.

By 6 months

You've recommended how to elevate RK's reporting, and we've agreed on a plan.
You've proposed a standard set of metrics and a consistent report format across ministries.
You've set up how client data is organized and protected, so cross-ministry benchmarking can be done responsibly.
Account leads bring you into client conversations because your recommendations go beyond the original request.

By 1 year

Standardized reporting with benchmarks is running as a new service for our ministry partners, allowing them to see how their experience fits within a larger ministry context. 
RK's data and reporting processes are documented and repeatable.
You’ve elevated reporting both internally and for our clients.

What you bring

Required

3–5 years of experience in data analysis, marketing analytics, reporting, or a similar role.
Well versed in using AI tools, such as Claude, in your daily work. 
Comfortable in Excel: pivot tables, lookups, and cleaning and combining messy data. You genuinely enjoy working in spreadsheets.
A track record of presenting findings and recommendations to non-technical audiences.
Clear, concise writing — you can explain what the data means and what to do about it.
Initiative: you find answers and solve problems without needing step-by-step direction.
Strong communication and people skills, including asking good questions and setting clear expectations.
Sound judgment with confidential information.
A general understanding of Christian denominational and theological differences, and empathy for the mission of non-profit ministries.

Preferred

Bachelor's degree, or trade school or certificate training, in a related field.
Experience with nonprofit fundraising, direct response, media buying, or donor data.
Familiarity with radio, podcast, or social media metrics.
Experience with SQL, or with a BI tool such as Power BI or Tableau. Experience setting up or managing a database.
Experience working with multiple clients/accounts at once.

Work environment and pay

Schedule:
In our Westlake Village office Tuesday through Thursday. Monday and Friday you can work from home or come into the office. Hours are 8:00 a.m.–5:00 p.m. Pacific.
Travel:
Occasional partner visits and an industry conference, up to about 5%.
Pay:
$80-$95K BOE
Benefits:
Health, dental and vision insurance; FSA; life insurance; 401(k) Safe Harbor plan during open enrollment after one year; 15 days of paid time off; 5 sick days; and paid holidays.
Equipment:
Laptop and monitor provided in the office.

How to apply

Submit your resume, a cover letter (required; one page maximum)
, and answers to the application questions. Applications without a cover letter won't be considered.

Strong communication and presentation skills, with the ability to collaborate effectively with technical and non-technical stakeholders.
